title: Simulator <-> coordinator loop
description: The coordinator runs as a subprocess of the simulator and speaks newline-delimited JSON (one message per line) on stdin/stdout; stderr is free for logs. Sequence: sim sends hello -> coordinator replies welcome -> repeat { sim sends observation(seq=n) -> coordinator replies decision(seq=n) } -> sim sends end. Sim time does not advance while the simulator waits for a decision. Either side may send error and exit. From 1.1, protocol versions with the same MAJOR are compatible: a coordinator ignores what it does not know in the simulator's messages, and sends only what the simulator's version defines (docs/semantics.md, section 1.6). These schemas are strict and describe exactly what version 1.1 sends, so validate a message against the schemas of the version that produced it.

Hello.description: First message. The coordinator must check protocol_version before reading the scenario. Goals are not part of the scenario: they arrive as earth_message events, the first at t = scenario.start_t.

site.description: Prior knowledge of the site (orbital data), not ground truth.

base_station.description: The site comms hub that defines robot coverage.

constants.description: Since 1.1. The simulator constants a coordinator plans with. A simulator on 1.1 or later always sends them; they are optional here so that a 1.0 scenario stays valid.

Constants.description: Simulator constants that a coordinator needs to plan. docs/semantics.md uses each where it applies, and its appendix lists them. Work is counted in the repair capability's unit (a health fraction) and is done at the executor's repair rate.

grade_window_m.description: `grade` only accepts a cell within this distance of its target elevation.

compaction_settlement_m.description: Mean distance a cell settles when it is compacted.

min_work_duration_s.description: The shortest any work step but loading and dumping can take.

rock_density_kg_m3.description: Density of boulders. A boulder is a sphere of rock, so its mass follows from its diameter.

repair_work_disabled.description: Repair work per disabled, field-repairable fault.

repair_work_stuck.description: Repair work to free a stuck robot.

repair_work_per_wear_removed.description: Repair work per unit of wear the repair removes.

repair_wear_removed_fraction.description: Fraction of each component's wear a repair removes.

strip_work.description: Work to strip a robot for parts.

tow_speed_factor.description: Speed of a tow as a fraction of the tower's max_speed_m_s.

tow_energy_factor.description: Drive energy of a tow as a multiple of the tower's drive_energy_wh_per_m.

depot_service_s.description: How long a depot service takes.

depot_capacity.description: Robots a depot services at once. The rest wait, first come, first served.

heater_threshold_c.description: Ambient temperature below which robot heaters run.

heater_power_factor.description: Heater draw as a multiple of the robot's idle_power_w, added to idle drain.

relay_radio_w.description: Radio power a robot draws while holding as a relay, on top of idle drain.

lost_link_timeout_s.description: How long an idle robot stays out of coverage before it drives back toward the base station on its own.

earth_response_mean_s.description: Mission control's mean time to answer an approval request once it arrives at Earth.

Observation.description: Sent at every decision point: a command completed, failed or was rejected, a fault, a weather/power/comms change, an Earth message arrived, or the coordinator's requested wake_at time was reached. docs/semantics.md lists them all.

seq.description: Starts at 0, increases by 1 per observation.

events.description: Events delivered since the previous observation, in the order they were delivered. Each keeps the time it happened, so events held back while a robot was out of coverage can be older than ones delivered before them.

robots.description: Current state of every robot as seen through (noisy) telemetry.

seq.description: Must echo the seq of the observation being answered.

to_earth.description: Messages queued for transmission to Earth.

wake_at.description: Request an observation at this time even if nothing happens.
